Two WHO AFRO-authored papers found by Agent 3 in Europe PMC cut in OPPOSITE directions and both are recorded here rather than only the convenient one. (1) CORROBORATING: BMJ Glob Health 2025;10:e016168 (WHO AFRO, PMC11759201) classifies 29 of the 47 African Region member states as cholera-endemic and places Mauritania explicitly in the NON-ENDEMIC group - 'the results for non-endemic countries like Central African Republic, Mauritania and South Africa, should be interpreted with caution ... non-endemic countries might not have prioritised cholera'. A WHO AFRO endemicity classification of non-endemic is positive institutional evidence of sustained absence, not merely missing data. (2) QUALIFYING: BMJ Glob Health 2025;10:e016491 (WHO AFRO, PMC11891530) states 'By 2002, 33 countries out of the 47 in the WHO African region had integrated cholera in their IDSR reporting. It is noticeable that cholera outbreaks have occurred in many countries that do not have cholera integrated in their surveillance system at some point (Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Eritrea, Gambia, Guinea Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritania, Niger, Rwanda).' Mauritania is named. The same paper adds that 'many countries in the past were reluctant to notify cholera ... and reported the disease as acute watery diarrhoea to WHO' until advocacy changed this from 2018. And e016168 scores Mauritania joint-LOWEST of 27 assessed countries on the 21-milestone regional cholera framework, at 19 percent. NET ADJUDICATION: the surveillance descriptor on this row is downgraded from 'operational' to PARTIAL. The row remains a Documented_Absence rather than a Surveillance_Gap, because Mauritania demonstrably retained a live WHO cholera notification channel across this block - it notified 46 cases in 2011 and appears with explicit tabulated zeros for 2009-2010 and 2012-2015 in Moore et al. PLoS NTD 2018 Table 1 - so this is a system that was looking and reporting nothing, not a system that had stopped reporting. But the evidence does NOT support a claim that cholera-specific surveillance was fully operational throughout, and a low-grade AWD-coded outbreak going unnotified cannot be excluded.
